title: Vanguard club insignia screen-print pack: neutralize six mixed-lighting mark captures to one house ink set and pin the club olive to one drab across every mark, then trace the badge into full-colour art plus one-colour spot plates, dual-trace the wordmark, deliver a webshop packshot of the jersey shot, and author a distressed tee graphic
grounding_note: ADAPTED from a real Upwork brief in which a youth/athletic team had mocked up a logo set with a general-purpose AI image tool and needed the messy raster art 'refined' into production formats 'for screen printing, social media, creating my own print graphics, etc.', delivered 'both vector based with separate layers and rasterized' with 'spot color info', in a muted military palette ('olive drab, khaki, black, dark grey' plus 'camo patterns, including digital camo') and a 'military type font'. The team is laundered to the fictional 'Vanguard' youth athletic club (a generic English word used as an invented team persona with a military-stencil aesthetic; unrelated to any real organisation, and no real nation, flag, team, player, product, software, or typeface is named or depicted anywhere in the task-facing fields). The AI tool of origin and any page-layout / illustration software names are removed; the original's real national-flag element is laundered to a generic 'subdued heraldic banner field'. REASONABLY ENRICHED into a runnable Adobe-connector benchmark AND repaired against the audit: (1) the earlier version 'locked each named element to a spot ink' via image_select_by_prompt -> image_fill_area, which only SOLID-fills a whole mask (it cannot produce a spot separation and destroys interior negative space) - that entire chain is removed; spot separations are now produced the honest connector way (a named-element SELECTION fed to image_vectorize returns that element's one-colour silhouette = its spot plate; the whole-emblem subject selection returns the registration plate; a whole-raster colour trace returns the full-colour art). (2) the earlier version shipped a hand-authored layered .ai as BOTH a supplied input AND a deliverable and 'exported' it with document_render_vector - a provenance dodge that laundered the composition work; the .ai and render_vector are removed entirely, mirroring the passing vectorize exemplars (image_vectorize honestly emits SVG). (3) the single amputated hero is restored to a real batch of SIX differently-lit mark captures, each carrying an in-frame 18% grey card, so cross-asset ink consistency becomes a trippable, gradeable craft target rather than a one-off. The client is modelled as supplying its mark set only as prints on existing gear and printed proofs, photographed across two sessions under different light, plus one decoy (the badge as screen-printed on a woven jersey) that looks like 'just another mark image' but must not be traced. All eight supplied files share a neutral, same-kind mark_ref naming scheme so which capture is the combined badge and which is the untraceable fabric photo is discoverable only by opening them - no supplied field encodes the triage.
one_line_ask: Turn the Vanguard club's six mixed-lighting mark captures into a production screen-print pack: neutralize every capture to one shared house white point by eye using its in-frame grey card and pin the club's olive to one consistent drab across every olive-bearing mark so the inks read identically across the set, trace the primary badge into full-colour vector art plus per-element one-colour spot plates and a registration plate, dual-trace the wordmark into art plus a one-colour cut plate, cut out the game-worn jersey shot as a 1600x2000 webshop packshot, vectorize the digital-camo accent, author a distressed tee graphic, recommend a stencil font, and hand back a spot-ink and applied-parameters reference sheet.
full_brief:
We run the Vanguard youth athletic club and our insignia set is a mess. It only exists as prints on our old gear and a few printed proof cards, and the shots we took of them don't match - they were photographed on different days under different light, so the same olive looks like three different olives across the pictures. On the edge of every shot we clipped a small neutral grey card and a white chip so the colour can be reconciled after the fact. We need this rebuilt into real, production-ready artwork we can hand a screen printer and also use online.

The non-negotiable bar: the whole set has to read as ONE brand in ONE ink set. Every mark must resolve to the same true, consistent inks from our palette - olive drab, khaki, black and dark grey - so our printer loads one set of inks and every garment matches. In particular our olive drab has to come out as the SAME olive on every mark that carries it, not a slightly different green each time. A set where each mark was just 'made to look nice on its own' will come back with mismatched olives and we'll reject it.

What we need back: for the primary combined badge, a clean scalable full-colour vector version of the whole mark AND the separations our printer actually burns - a one-colour plate for the standout element and a single-colour registration plate for the whole emblem. For our wordmark lockup, both a full-colour vector version and a single-colour cut version for one-ink jobs. Take the shot of the badge as it appears heat-pressed on one of our jerseys and give us a clean product cut-out on white for the webshop at 1600x2000. Vectorize our digital-camo swatch into a repeatable accent. Give us one distressed, worn-in version of the badge we can drop straight onto a vintage-look tee. Recommend a military/stencil-style font that suits the wordmark. And hand back a one-page reference sheet listing which single ink each separation represents, the shared house white point everything was matched to, and - per capture - the white-balance and exposure moves you settled on, so we can trust the set really is one matched ink set and not eyeballed shot by shot. Keep the marks separable so we can re-edit outline, stroke and fill later.

inputs.name: mark_ref_01.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat top-down photograph of a printed proof card of an athletic team emblem badge: a circular outer olive-drab ring with a condensed uppercase military-stencil 'VANGUARD' wordmark band across the bottom; inside the ring a subdued heraldic banner field of muted horizontal bars, a single five-point khaki star, three downward dark-grey chevrons, and a stylised left-facing sentinel head silhouette. Palette restricted to olive drab green, khaki tan, black and dark grey, printed flat on white card. The capture is under WARM gym tungsten light (about 3200K, a clear amber cast), a touch underexposed and dull/low-contrast, and the whole card is rotated about +3 degrees clockwise so the baselines are not level. In the bottom margin, print a small neutral 18% grey calibration square and a white chip and four black corner registration ticks. Documentary print-proof realism, no CGI gloss, flat art, 3000x3000.
inputs.realism_notes: REFERENCE mark and the frame that sets the house look - the ONLY capture carrying every element, so which of the eight files is the combined badge is discoverable only by opening them. Warm amber cast (~3200K), dull/underexposed, tilted ~+3deg - so it needs a straighten, a warm->neutral white-balance move judged on its in-frame 18% grey card BY EYE (the agent never reads a channel/hex value; it dials until the card looks neutral and reports what it dialed), and an authored muted-drab olive grade that becomes the shared target the other olive-bearing marks are pinned to. It carries every element (banner field, star, chevrons, sentinel head, wordmark band, outer ring), so it is where the per-element one-colour spot plate and the whole-emblem registration plate are pulled, and where the full-colour art trace comes from. Traceable flat proof. The grey card is cropped OUT before tracing but retained on the neutralized master for QC.

inputs.name: mark_ref_02.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat top-down photograph of a printed proof card showing a horizontal team wordmark lockup: the single word 'VANGUARD' in a bold condensed uppercase military-stencil face, printed solid khaki tan with a thin dark-grey keyline, on white card. Under WARM gym tungsten light (about 3200K, amber cast), slightly dull. In the bottom margin a small neutral 18% grey calibration square, a white chip, and four corner registration ticks. Documentary print-proof realism, flat art, legible lettering, no CGI, 3000x1400.
inputs.realism_notes: Traceable flat proof, SAME warm session as the badge. Carries NO olive (khaki lettering + dark-grey keyline only), so it gets white-balance neutralization but no house-olive pass. Gets a full-colour art trace AND a one-colour cut/spot plate from the SAME cleaned raster - a whole-raster colour trace versus a lettering-SELECTION fed to image_vectorize (which returns a single-colour silhouette). Swap the two polarities and the art loses its keyline or the cut plate arrives as un-burnable two-colour art. Its warm cast must be corrected to the SAME house white point as the badge, not to its own pleasing white. Text-bearing mark, so the legible-lettering model is used; still a photograph of a flat print.

inputs.name: mark_ref_03.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat top-down photograph of a printed proof card showing a single five-point khaki star icon with a thin olive-drab outline, printed flat on white card. Under WARM gym tungsten light (about 3200K, amber cast), slightly dull. In the bottom margin a small neutral 18% grey calibration square, a white chip, and four corner registration ticks. Documentary print-proof realism, flat art, no CGI, 3000x3000.
inputs.realism_notes: Traceable flat proof, warm session. Part of the matched-set consistency batch AND an olive-bearing mark: its warm cast must be pulled to the SAME house white point as the badge, and its thin olive-drab outline must then get the SAME authored house-olive pass (green-band desaturate-and-darken) applied to the badge in the workflow, or its olive prints a different green than the badge's even after white-balance. Delivered as a matched cleaned raster (card cropped), with its card-bearing neutralized+authored master retained for QC.

inputs.name: mark_ref_04.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A photoreal flat-lay product photograph of the team badge as it appears heat-pressed on a heather-grey woven athletic jersey, laid on a smooth light studio sweep and shot slightly from above. The emblem sits on real woven polyester fabric with visible knit texture, soft folds, wrinkles and specular sheen catching the light; a soft contact shadow on the sweep. The jersey is the clear centred subject. Documentary catalogue realism, real fabric, no CGI gloss, 3000x3750.
inputs.realism_notes: TRIAGE DECOY. Sharing the neutral mark_ref scheme, it looks like 'another badge image' but it is the emblem screen-printed on folded, textured woven fabric - it CANNOT be traced (weave, folds, perspective and sheen become garbage paths). Its only correct use is the webshop packshot: knock the studio sweep to transparency with image_remove_background, then downscale/reframe to the 1600x2000 product tile (a pure downscale from the 3000x3750 source - never an upscale or canvas-extend). A naive agent that runs it through the same select->vectorize path it just used on the flat proofs produces an unusable trace, invisible until the SVG path data is opened. Not part of the white-point batch (a garment photo, not a card-bearing proof), and not an olive-authored mark.

inputs.name: mark_ref_05.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat top-down photograph of a printed proof card showing three stacked downward dark-grey chevrons with olive-drab spacing, printed flat on white card. This capture is under COOL north-window daylight (about 5600K, a clear blue cast) and is noticeably BRIGHTER than the warm-session cards. In the bottom margin a small neutral 18% grey calibration square, a white chip, and four corner registration ticks. Documentary print-proof realism, flat art, no CGI, 3000x2000.
inputs.realism_notes: Traceable flat proof, COOL daylight (~5600K, blue cast) and brighter than the warm session - so its correct move is the OPPOSITE of the badge/wordmark: warm the white balance and pull exposure DOWN to reach the SAME house white point. Copying the badge's cooling numbers here leaves it off-neutral and its dark grey / olive print a different shade than the warm marks - the consistency trap. It is ALSO olive-bearing (olive-drab spacing between the chevrons), so after white-balance it must get the SAME authored house-olive pass as the badge so its olive resolves to the identical drab. Delivered as a matched cleaned raster; card-bearing neutralized+authored master retained for QC.

inputs.name: mark_ref_06.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat top-down photograph of a printed proof card showing a stylised left-facing sentinel head silhouette in dark grey with a khaki highlight edge, printed flat on white card. Under COOL north-window daylight (about 5600K, blue cast), a little bright. In the bottom margin a small neutral 18% grey calibration square, a white chip, and four corner registration ticks. Documentary print-proof realism, flat art, no CGI, 3000x3000.
inputs.realism_notes: Traceable flat proof, cool session - an opposite-direction white-balance correction (warm it, pull down) to the same house white point. Carries NO olive (dark grey with a khaki highlight edge), so it gets white-balance neutralization but no house-olive pass. Part of the consistency batch; delivered as a matched cleaned raster, card-bearing master retained for QC.

inputs.name: mark_ref_07.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat top-down photograph of a printed proof card showing the outer badge ring and centre monogram alone: a circular olive-drab ring enclosing a khaki 'V' monogram, printed flat on white card. Under COOL north-window daylight (about 5600K, blue cast), a little bright and flat. In the bottom margin a small neutral 18% grey calibration square, a white chip, and four corner registration ticks. Documentary print-proof realism, flat art, no CGI, 3000x3000.
inputs.realism_notes: Traceable flat proof, cool session - opposite-direction correction to the same house white point. Its olive ring is the most sensitive check for a residual cast because olive drifts obviously if the white point is wrong. It is olive-bearing, so after white-balance it must get the SAME authored house-olive pass as the badge so its ring resolves to the identical drab - if it is neutralized but NOT olive-authored, its ring reads a different green from the badge's olive and the one-ink-set bar fails. Part of the consistency batch; delivered as a matched cleaned raster, card-bearing neutralized+authored master retained for QC.

inputs.name: digital_camo_swatch.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A seamless digital pixel-camouflage pattern swatch of blocky pixel clusters in olive drab green, khaki tan, dark grey and black, flat even lighting, no logo, no text, square tile, high-contrast and clean so it can be vectorized into a repeatable accent fill, 2048x2048.
inputs.realism_notes: A flat, high-contrast pixel-camo tile, no people or text - clean enough to vectorize into a repeatable accent fill. Not part of the white-point consistency batch and not olive-authored; a straightforward whole-raster trace.

outputs.name: matched_neutralized_masters
outputs.spec: The six mark captures (badge, wordmark, star, chevron, head, ring) after straightening (where needed) and white-balance/tone neutralization to ONE shared house white point - and, for the four olive-bearing marks (badge, star, chevron, ring), the SAME authored house-olive pass so their olive resolves to one drab - each WITH its in-frame 18% grey card still in frame. Retained as the QC artifact where the grader measures neutrality/consistency (the agent neutralized by eye and never measured). These are the card-BEARING masters; neutrality tolerance and olive consistency are checked here, not on the cropped production files.

outputs.name: cleaned_mark_set
outputs.spec: The same six marks cropped to their own bounds so the grey card and registration ticks are OUT of frame - clean, white-point-matched production rasters the printer can place directly. Card-exclusion is checked on these files; because all six were driven to one white point and every olive-bearing mark got the same authored house-olive pass, the club's inks - olive included - read identically across the set.

outputs.name: badge_art.svg
outputs.spec: Full-colour scalable vector art of the primary combined badge, whole-raster colour-traced from the cleaned, neutralized, authored-look badge master by image_vectorize - the olive ring, khaki star, dark-grey chevrons and other inks coming through as separate closed shapes so outline/stroke/fill stay re-editable.

outputs.name: chevron_spot_plate.svg
outputs.spec: One-colour spot plate of the badge's chevron element: a single solid silhouette produced by feeding the chevron SELECTION (image_select_by_prompt on the cleaned badge) to image_vectorize, which returns a one-colour silhouette. This is the honest connector spot-separation mechanic - not a fill_area solid-fill. On a light garment its counters read as the ground; it is NOT claimed as an enclosed-hole knockout on a dark ground.

outputs.name: badge_registration_plate.svg
outputs.spec: Single-colour registration plate for the whole emblem: the badge-subject selection (image_select_subject) fed to image_vectorize, returning one solid silhouette of the entire mark for press registration / the black separation. A one-colour vector, not a filled photo.

outputs.name: wordmark_art.svg
outputs.spec: Full-colour scalable vector art of the wordmark lockup, whole-raster colour-traced from its cleaned master by image_vectorize - khaki lettering and dark-grey keyline as separate shapes. Weight- and white-point-matched to badge_art.svg because both were neutralized to the same house white point.

outputs.name: wordmark_cut_plate.svg
outputs.spec: One-colour cut/spot plate of the wordmark: the lettering SELECTION fed to image_vectorize returning a single solid silhouette (fill + keyline collapsed to one colour) for one-ink jobs and clean plotter weeding. The mask-polarity partner of wordmark_art.svg from the SAME cleaned raster.

outputs.name: jersey_packshot_web.jpg
outputs.spec: Webshop product cut-out of the game-worn badge capture: the studio sweep knocked out by image_remove_background and the subject reframed/downscaled to exactly 1600x2000, sRGB, on white. A RASTER packshot with NO vector paths - this file proves the fabric photo was correctly triaged as a photograph, not traced. A pure downscale from the 3000x3750 source.

outputs.name: camo_accent.svg
outputs.spec: Vectorized digital-camo swatch (image_vectorize whole-raster trace) as a clean, repeatable vector accent fill.

outputs.name: vintage_merch_hero.png
outputs.spec: An authored distressed tee graphic the agent OWNS: the cleaned badge given a halftone screen-print dot texture (image_apply_halftone) then a distress grain pass (image_add_grain) at the agent's chosen intensity, producing a worn-in vintage-athletic print on a light/heather ground. Its distinctive quality is the agent's decision, not a client template or a canned preset default. Kept on a light ground - not claimed as a dark-ground knockout.

outputs.name: stencil_font_pairing.json
outputs.spec: Recommended military/stencil-style font family whose proportions suit the wordmark (font_recommend). Recommendation of an existing family only - no from-scratch letterform design.

outputs.name: ink_and_params_report.txt
outputs.spec: Agent-authored one-page reference sheet: which single ink each separation (chevron spot plate, registration plate, wordmark cut plate) represents; the one shared house white point all six captures were matched to; the one authored house olive every olive-bearing mark was pinned to; and, per capture, the white-balance (temperature/tint) and exposure moves the agent dialed - an applied-settings log, NOT a measured/recovered value. This is the acceptance artifact that makes 'one matched ink set' checkable, and the reported corrections must be non-identical between the warm and cool captures.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: mark_ref_01.png, mark_ref_02.png, mark_ref_03.png, mark_ref_04.png, mark_ref_05.png, mark_ref_06.png, mark_ref_07.png, digital_camo_swatch.png
connector_workflow.note: Single asset load: bring the seven neutrally-named mark captures and the digital-camo swatch into Creative Cloud storage. Which file is the combined badge (mark_ref_01) and which is the untraceable game-worn fabric photo (mark_ref_04) is decided only by opening them. Every later step consumes a named prior output; this is the only ingest.
Level the tilt on the primary badge capture (mark_ref_01, the one carrying every element) so element edges are square before any grading or tracing. Report the correcting angle used.

Neutralize the primary badge capture by eye, judging its in-frame grey card until it LOOKS neutral and the white chip reads as a true white, and set a dark, separable tone so the flat inks read cleanly. This capture's settling defines the shared HOUSE WHITE POINT the rest of the set must hit. The agent never reads a pixel or channel value - it dials by eye and REPORTS the temperature/tint/exposure/blacks it chose. Not a preset, not auto-tone.

Author the house olive from primitives: pin the club's olive to one consistent muted service-drab by a reasoned per-hue-band move (desaturate and darken the green band, hold the khaki/yellow band) so the traced fills are crisp and on-brand. A judged authored grade within the tool's range - no near-complementary rotation - not a preset. This DEFINES the single authored house olive; the same green-band move is re-applied to every other olive-bearing mark (steps 7, 9, 12) so all four olives resolve identically. This master is the target for the set and the source of the badge separations.

Neutralize the wordmark capture (mark_ref_02, warm session) by eye to the SAME house white point set in step 3, judging its own in-frame grey card. It carries no olive, so no house-olive pass is applied. Report the temperature/tint/exposure you dialed for this capture; they are its own correction, not a copy of the badge's.

Neutralize the star capture (mark_ref_03, warm session) by eye to the shared house white point using its in-frame grey card. Report the parameters applied. It is olive-bearing (thin olive outline), so it continues to the house-olive pass in step 7.

Author the house olive on the star: apply the SAME green-band desaturate-and-darken move used on the badge in step 4 so the star's olive outline resolves to the identical house drab. Without this authored pass, white-balance alone leaves its olive off the badge's olive and the set fails the one-ink-set bar. Within image_adjust_hsl's range - no near-complementary rotation, not a preset.

Neutralize the chevron capture (mark_ref_05) by eye to the shared house white point using its in-frame grey card. It is a COOL, brighter capture, so its correction is the OPPOSITE direction to the warm marks - warm the balance and pull exposure DOWN; copying the badge's cooling numbers leaves it off-neutral. Report the parameters applied. Olive-bearing (olive spacing), so it continues to the house-olive pass in step 9.

Author the house olive on the chevron mark: apply the SAME green-band desaturate-and-darken move used on the badge in step 4 so the chevron's olive spacing resolves to the identical house drab. Within image_adjust_hsl's range - no near-complementary rotation, not a preset.

Neutralize the sentinel-head capture (mark_ref_06, cool session) by eye to the shared house white point using its in-frame grey card - an opposite-direction correction (warm it, pull down). It carries no olive, so no house-olive pass is applied. Report the parameters applied.

Neutralize the ring/monogram capture (mark_ref_07, cool session) by eye to the shared house white point using its in-frame grey card - an opposite-direction correction (warm it, pull down); its olive ring is the most sensitive residual-cast check. Report the parameters applied. Olive-bearing, so it continues to the house-olive pass in step 12. Steps 3-4, 5, 6-7, 8-9, 10 and 11-12 together produce the matched_neutralized_masters set (card in frame) the grader checks for one common white point AND one house olive.

Author the house olive on the ring/monogram mark: apply the SAME green-band desaturate-and-darken move used on the badge in step 4 so the olive ring resolves to the identical house drab. If neutralized but NOT olive-authored, the ring reads a different green from the badge's olive and the one-ink-set bar fails. Within image_adjust_hsl's range - no near-complementary rotation, not a preset.

Crop the neutralized authored-look badge to the emblem bounds, dropping the grey card, white chip and registration ticks so the trace sees only artwork on clean white. Report the crop bounds. Production-clean badge master.
Crop the neutralized wordmark to its lettering bounds, dropping the card and ticks. Production-clean wordmark master and the source for its dual trace.
Crop the neutralized, olive-authored star to bounds, dropping the card and ticks. Matched cleaned production raster (part of cleaned_mark_set), its olive pinned to the house drab.
Crop the neutralized, olive-authored chevron mark to bounds, dropping the card and ticks. Matched cleaned production raster, its olive spacing pinned to the house drab.
Crop the neutralized sentinel-head mark to bounds, dropping the card and ticks. Matched cleaned production raster (no olive to author).

Crop the neutralized, olive-authored ring/monogram mark to bounds, dropping the card and ticks. Matched cleaned production raster completing the cleaned_mark_set, its olive ring pinned to the house drab.
Full-colour art: whole-raster colour-trace the cleaned, neutralized, authored-look badge so its inks come through as separate closed shapes. No selection - this is the multi-ink art path.
Select the chevron element by name on the cleaned badge to isolate it as one shape for its own separation. Semantic selection of a named element - not a hue or a region.

Spot plate: vectorize the chevron SELECTION, which returns a single solid one-colour silhouette - the printer's spot separation for that ink. This is the honest connector spot-plate mechanic (selection -> silhouette), distinct from the whole-raster colour trace in step 19.
Select the whole badge emblem as the subject on the cleaned badge to drive the single-colour registration plate.

Registration plate: vectorize the whole-emblem SELECTION to one solid silhouette of the entire mark for press registration / the black separation. Selection -> silhouette again, at the whole-mark scale.

Full-colour art for the wordmark: whole-raster colour-trace of the cleaned wordmark so the khaki lettering and dark-grey keyline are separate shapes. Because both it and the badge were neutralized to one white point, its inks match the badge art.
Select the wordmark lettering by name on the SAME cleaned wordmark raster used in step 24 - the mask-polarity partner input for the one-colour cut plate.

Cut/spot plate: vectorize the lettering SELECTION to a single solid silhouette (fill + keyline collapsed to one colour) for one-ink jobs. Same cleaned raster as step 24, deliberately the OTHER vectorize use (selection -> silhouette versus whole-raster colour trace).

Triage branch - the CORRECT treatment for the game-worn badge photo (mark_ref_04). It is a photograph of the emblem on folded, textured fabric, so it is NOT traced; instead knock the studio sweep to transparency, isolating the jersey subject as a clean cut-out. Feeding this file to image_vectorize as the flat proofs were would produce garbage weave/fold paths.

Webshop packshot: subject-aware reframe + downscale of the jersey cut-out to exactly 1600x2000, sRGB, on white. A pure downscale from the 3000x3750 source - never canvas-extend, never upscale. A raster deliverable with no vector paths, proving the photo was triaged away from the tracer.
Vectorize the flat, high-contrast digital-camo swatch (whole-raster trace) into a clean repeatable vector accent fill.

Author the distressed tee look, step one: apply a halftone screen-print dot texture to the cleaned badge at the agent's chosen treatment. An authored creative decision toward a worn vintage-athletic print, on a light ground.

Author the distressed tee look, step two: add a distress grain pass at the agent's chosen intensity, finishing the worn-in vintage merch graphic. The agent owns this artifact's distinctive quality - not a client template, not a canned preset default.
Recommend a military/stencil-style font whose proportions suit the wordmark, reading the wordmark art's style. Recommendation of an existing family only - no from-scratch letterform design.

chaining_note: Single ingest at step 1 (assets_uploaded); every later step consumes a named prior output. REFERENCE + AUTHOR-LOOK sub-chain forks from the badge (mark_ref_01): auto_straighten(2) -> apply_adjustments(3, neutralize the badge grey card by eye to set the shared house white point) -> adjust_hsl(4, author the muted-drab house olive) = badge_ref, the target and the source of the badge separations. The house olive authored in step 4 is re-applied identically to every other olive-bearing mark so all four olives resolve to one drab: star apply_adjustments(6)->adjust_hsl(7)=star_ref, chevron apply_adjustments(8)->adjust_hsl(9)=chevron_ref, ring apply_adjustments(11)->adjust_hsl(12)=ring_ref; the two non-olive marks get white-balance only - wordmark apply_adjustments(5)=wordmark_neutral, head apply_adjustments(10)=head_neutral. Each apply_adjustments is a DIFFERENT by-eye correction to the SAME white point (three warm: badge/wordmark/star; three cool: chevron/head/ring). badge_ref, wordmark_neutral, star_ref, chevron_ref, head_neutral and ring_ref (all card-bearing) are the matched_neutralized_masters the grader checks for one common white point and one house olive. SIX crop_to_bounds(13-18) drop each card off its master to make the card-excluded cleaned_mark_set (badge_clean and wordmark_clean also seed the traces). BADGE separations off badge_clean: whole-raster colour trace(19)=badge_art.svg, select chevron(20)->vectorize silhouette(21)=chevron_spot_plate.svg, select_subject(22)->vectorize silhouette(23)=badge_registration_plate.svg. WORDMARK dual trace off wordmark_clean: whole-raster colour trace(24)=wordmark_art.svg and select lettering(25)->vectorize silhouette(26)=wordmark_cut_plate.svg (the mask-polarity pair from one raster). TRIAGE branch takes the game-worn photo (mark_ref_04) a deliberately different way: remove_background(27) then crop_and_resize(28) to the 1600x2000 packshot - never the tracer. camo swatch trace(29)=camo_accent.svg. OWNED artifact off badge_clean: halftone(30)->add_grain(31)=vintage_merch_hero.png. font_recommend(32) reads the wordmark art. The eight inputs share a neutral mark_ref_01..07 scheme (plus the camo swatch), so which capture is the combined badge and which is the untraceable fabric photo is discoverable only by inspection - no filename, title or one_line_ask encodes it. No .ai and no document_render_vector: every vector emerges honestly from image_vectorize. Cross-asset consistency is NOT one recipe repeated - the six white-balance corrections share only the white point, the four olive-authoring passes share only the house drab, and the agent reports every setting so the match is auditable.
difficulty_rationale: Depth, not breadth: 32 dependent connector calls across 13 distinct Adobe tools, but the difficulty is in the reasoning.
